idiom: bite off more than you can chew
meaning: to try to do more work than you are able to manage
literal_translation: wziąć na siebie więcej, niż się jest w stanie udźwignąć
example: I signed up for five extra classes this term and bit off more than I could chew.
origin: Comes from the image of taking a bite of food that is too big to chew.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to eat a meal much too quickly
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about taking on too many tasks, not about how fast you eat.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to be careless about your teeth
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with dental care or health.
The idiom describes accepting too much work, not refusing food.

explanation: 'Bite off more than you can chew' comes from the image of a bite of food that is too big to chew. It means to take on more work or responsibility than you can manage.
